title: AdaOcc: Adaptive 3D Occupancy Prediction for Embodied Tasks
claim: One adaptive perception module accepts heterogeneous robot sensors and budgets, and outputs structured semantic 3D predictions for diverse downstream embodied tasks.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, colored arrows linking sensors, model, prediction, tasks
description: A wide four-panel figure read left to right. The leftmost panel, 'Heterogeneous Robots & Sensors', lists humanoid, wheeled-arm and quadruped robot photos beside three inputs: RGB multi-view images (blue frame), depth maps (green, dashed arrow) and LiDAR scans (orange, dashed arrow). Arrows lead into the central 'AdaOcc' panel. It shows a small diagram of query points and an encoder feeding a stack of decoder layers 1 to N. Below it are three rounded badges: View-adaptive, Sensor-adaptive and Budget-adaptive. A big dark purple arrow leads to the 'Semantic 3D Prediction' panel. That panel shows a sparse colored point cloud and the matching dense semantic occupancy, linked by pink cyclic arrows, with a legend (table, chair, wall, monitor, floor). The rightmost column holds three downstream task cards: navigation, manipulation and mobile manipulation.
caption: Overview of AdaOcc. AdaOcc targets adaptive 3D occupancy prediction for embodied scene understanding. It accepts heterogeneous visual and geometric inputs from different embodied platforms and adapts to different computational budgets through adjustable query numbers and decoder depths. AdaOcc predicts sparse semantic points, which can be converted into semantic occupancy to provide structured spatial cues for downstream embodied tasks.
abstract: Embodied tasks demand accurate, flexible, and semantically rich 3D scene representations. 3D semantic occupancy is well suited to this requirement, as it can model holistic 3D spaces by encoding geometric occupancy along with semantic categories. However, existing occupancy prediction methods struggle to meet practical deployment requirements, such as adapting to varying computing budgets, sensor setups, and observation views. In this paper, we propose a point-based Adaptive 3D Occupancy Prediction method, called AdaOcc, tailored for embodied scenarios. To accommodate heterogeneous sensor inputs, AdaOcc uses an adaptive geometry-guided dual-branch encoder that can support RGB images in various numbers of views with (estimated) depth maps or LiDAR scans. AdaOcc represents occupied regions via sparse semantic points trained with a progressive query learning strategy, allowing the prediction computational budget to be flexibly adjusted through query point numbers and decoder layers. To facilitate high-fidelity geometric modeling for lightweight point-based occupancy learning, we further propose a novel containment loss that regularizes predicted points to reside within valid occupied regions. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves a new state-of-the-art on Occ-ScanNet with considerable performance improvements over previous methods. Moreover, our framework demonstrates strong practical applicability as an adaptive 3D perception module in real-world embodied systems.
